reference.source: Kanski Clinical Ophthalmology / Cornea by Krachmer
clinicalPearls: An autosomal dominant stromal dystrophy showing discrete white crumb- or breadcrumb-like granular opacities in the central anterior stroma with clear intervening spaces
Caused by mutations in the TGFBI gene on chromosome 5q31, sharing its locus with lattice and Reis-Bucklers dystrophies
The hyaline deposits stain bright red with Masson trichrome on histology
Vision is often preserved until later life because the clear stroma between deposits maintains transparency
Type 2 (Avellino / combined granular-lattice) shows both hyaline granular and amyloid lattice deposits and stains with both Masson trichrome and Congo red
Recurrent erosions may occur but are generally less troublesome than in lattice or Reis-Bucklers dystrophy
Management ranges from lubrication for erosions to phototherapeutic keratectomy or lamellar/penetrating keratoplasty for significant visual loss
Deposits characteristically recur in the subepithelial and anterior stromal graft after keratoplasty
reference.pathophysiology: Granular corneal dystrophy is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by mutations in the transforming growth factor beta-induced gene (TGFBI). The mutant protein misfolds and accumulates as hyaline deposits within the corneal stroma, appearing as discrete granular opacities separated by clear stroma. Over time deposits enlarge and become more numerous, and superficial deposits can disrupt epithelial adhesion. In the type 2 combined form, the same gene produces both hyaline (granular) and amyloid (lattice) material, giving a mixed histological picture. Progressive accumulation eventually reduces transparency and vision.
additionalDifferentials: Lattice corneal dystrophy and combined granular-lattice (Avellino) dystrophy
Stromal scarring or infiltrates from prior keratitis
additionalInvestigations: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy documenting discrete granular opacities with clear intervening stroma
Histology with Masson trichrome staining of hyaline deposits
TGFBI genetic testing to confirm subtype and identify combined granular-lattice disease
Congo red staining to detect coexistent amyloid in suspected type 2 disease
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography to assess deposit depth
Corneal topography and pachymetry before surgical intervention
redFlags: Marked visual decline from confluent central deposits
Painful recurrent epithelial breakdown with risk of secondary infection
Rapid or atypically severe progression suggesting combined granular-lattice disease
Early recurrence of deposits within a graft compromising vision
reference.prognosis: Vision is often good for many years because clear stroma separates the deposits, but progressive accumulation may eventually require surgery. Deposits commonly recur after keratoplasty, and the combined type 2 form tends to be more visually significant.
pitfalls: Confusing granular deposits with infiltrates and treating as infective keratitis
Missing coexistent amyloid that reclassifies the disease as combined granular-lattice type
Assuming a graft will remain clear and not warning of deposit recurrence
Overlooking the autosomal dominant inheritance and failing to counsel family members
references: Cornea by Krachmer, Mannis and Holland
management: Observe asymptomatic or mildly affected eyes, as clear stroma between deposits preserves vision for many years
Relieve recurrent epithelial erosions with ocular lubricants, hypertonic saline, a bandage contact lens and epithelial debridement
Use excimer laser phototherapeutic keratectomy to remove visually significant superficial anterior stromal deposits
Reserve lamellar or penetrating keratoplasty for advanced deeper opacity causing marked visual loss
Counsel that deposits commonly recur in the graft and plan for repeat phototherapeutic keratectomy or regrafting
Avoid refractive laser surgery, which can accelerate deposition, particularly in the combined type 2 (Avellino) form
Offer genetic counselling for autosomal dominant inheritance and TGFBI testing to subtype disease and screen relatives
